title: The Subjunctive after أَنْ، لَنْ، كَيْ and حَتَّى
lede: Control regular, five-verb and weak-verb subjunctive forms after the main particles of intention, negation, purpose and endpoint.

items.prompt: Choose “I study in order to succeed”.
items.feedback: لِكَيْ introduces purpose and a subjunctive verb.

items.prompt: Choose “I wait until the bus arrives”.
items.feedback: Purpose/endpoint حَتَّى can govern the subjunctive.
The nūn drops from the five-verb form after أَنْ.

options: Not every حَتَّى automatically creates the same analysis; teach clear purpose/endpoint examples.
Every word after حتى is past.
The subjunctive never changes plural forms.
items.feedback: Meaning and syntax determine the structure.

items.prompt: I train so that I improve
I want you f. to study
I want the two students to arrive
I want the girls to write

items.feedback: Subjunctive written like indicative for final alif maqṣūra.

items.prompt: He studies so that he may come

blocks: ## Why this matters لِمَاذَا نَسْتَعْمِلُ الْمَنْصُوبَ؟
The subjunctive lets learners express what they want, need, intend, refuse and act in order to achieve.
### Core
Use أن and لن with common singular forms.
### Develop
Apply nūn deletion to the five verbs and use purpose clauses.
### Stretch
Contrast weak subjunctive and jussive forms and analyse endpoint structures.
[callout] Communication target: Build extended answers with intention, necessity, purpose and future negation.
## Diagnostic start
Identify the form required by each trigger.
## The main subjunctive triggers
Learn the particle together with its communicative function and model sentence.

TABLE: Particle | Function | Model // أَنْ | that / to after wanting, liking, needing, trying | أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَدْرُسَ. // لَنْ | future negation | لَنْ أَتَأَخَّرَ. // كَيْ / لِكَيْ | so that / in order to | أَتَدَرَّبُ لِكَيْ أَتَحَسَّنَ. // حَتَّى | until / so that in a clear endpoint or purpose relation | أَنْتَظِرُ حَتَّى يَصِلَ الْقِطَارُ.
[callout] Core visible sign: In fully supported regular singular forms, final ـُ changes to ـَ : أَدْرُسُ ← أَنْ أَدْرُسَ .
## Regular and five-verb endings
Subjunctive changes are especially visible in dual and masculine/feminine addressee plural forms.

TABLE: Indicative | Subjunctive | Reason // يَكْتُبُ | أَنْ يَكْتُبَ | regular singular final vowel // تَكْتُبِينَ | أَنْ تَكْتُبِي | five-verb nūn drops // يَكْتُبَانِ | أَنْ يَكْتُبَا | dual nūn drops // يَكْتُبُونَ | أَنْ يَكْتُبُوا | plural nūn drops // تَكْتُبْنَ | أَنْ تَكْتُبْنَ | feminine plural remains built on sukūn
[callout/warning] The “five verbs”: forms ending in ـانِ، ـونَ، ـينَ lose the nūn in the subjunctive. Do not remove the nūn from feminine plural تَكْتُبْنَ / يَكْتُبْنَ .
## Weak verbs in the subjunctive
Subjunctive and jussive weak forms must not be confused.

TABLE: Indicative | Subjunctive model | Note // يَرْمِي | لَنْ يَرْمِيَ | final y remains and takes visible fatḥa // يَدْعُو | لَنْ يَدْعُوَ | final wāw remains and takes visible fatḥa // يَسْعَى | لَنْ يَسْعَى | written form unchanged; the ending is estimated // يَرَى | أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَرَى | written alif maqṣūra remains // يَأْتِي | لِكَيْ يَأْتِيَ | final y takes fatḥa
[callout] Do not copy the jussive rule into the subjunctive. Compare لَمْ يَرْمِ (jussive) with لَنْ يَرْمِيَ (subjunctive).
## Subjunctive clauses express purpose and intention
These structures are productive tools for extended answers across topic areas.
### Want / intend
أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَعْمَلَ فِي الطِّبِّ.
### Need / obligation
يَجِبُ أَنْ نَحْمِيَ الْبِيئَةَ.
### Purpose
أَتَعَلَّمُ الْعَرَبِيَّةَ لِكَيْ أَتَوَاصَلَ مَعَ الْآخَرِينَ.
### Endpoint
سَأَنْتَظِرُ حَتَّى تَنْتَهِيَ الْحِصَّةُ.
[callout] Range without decoration: Subjunctive clauses add purpose, intention and necessity. Use them because the meaning requires them, not merely to appear complex.
## Subjunctive misconception clinic
A useful correction explains the form, not only the answer.
### After أن
✗ أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَدْرُسُ
✓ أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَدْرُسَ
Regular singular takes final fatḥa in the fully supported model.
### Five-verb nūn
✗ أُرِيدُكِ أَنْ تَكْتُبِينَ
✓ أُرِيدُكِ أَنْ تَكْتُبِي
The nūn drops.
### Jussive versus subjunctive
✗ لَنْ يَمْشِ
✓ لَنْ يَمْشِيَ
The subjunctive retains final y; the jussive drops it.
### Purpose structure
✗ أَدْرُسُ لِكَيْ نَجَحْتُ
✓ أَدْرُسُ لِكَيْ أَنْجَحَ
Purpose refers to the intended result, so use the subjunctive present.
## Replayable transformer
Change indicative forms into accurate subjunctives.
## Apply the grammar across skills
Grammar becomes useful when it helps you understand and communicate.
### 📖 Reading workshop
Read ambition profiles and underline triggers. Match each subordinate verb to the word that governs it.
### 🎧 Listening workshop
Listen for the difference between يكتبون / أن يكتبوا and يمشي / لن يمشيَ.
### 🗣️ Speaking workshop
Give a one-minute answer about a goal using أريد أن، يجب أن، لكي، لن and حتى.
### 🛠️ Editing workshop
Repair a paragraph with retained nūn, indicative endings after triggers and jussive forms used after لن.
### ✍️ Integrated production task
Write 130–140 words about your ambitions and what you do to achieve them. Include intention, necessity, purpose, future negation and an endpoint.

[callout] Model: أُرِيدُ أَنْ أُصْبِحَ مُهَنْدِسَةً، وَلِذَلِكَ يَجِبُ أَنْ أَدْرُسَ الرِّيَاضِيَّاتِ بِجِدٍّ. أَتَدَرَّبُ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ لِكَيْ أَتَحَسَّنَ، وَلَنْ أَتَوَقَّفَ حَتَّى أَحْقِّقَ هَدَفِي.
[callout] Success checklist: Use four different triggers, two five-verb forms and one weak verb; check the ending after every trigger.
Save and mark complete Clear
Plan the verb changes as a timeline, root map or sentence flowchart. Label each form in Arabic.
Make a trigger-to-verb arrow for every subjunctive clause. Label whether the visible change is fatḥa, nūn deletion or a weak-verb form.
## Final mastery check
Apply the subjunctive after its main triggers.
### Lesson mastery summary
- recognise the main subjunctive triggers;
- change regular and five-verb endings accurately;
- distinguish weak subjunctive forms from jussive forms;
- use purpose, intention and necessity clauses in connected language.
Return in 3–7 days and repeat the final check without reviewing first. Retrieval, not recognition alone, builds secure verb control.
